summary: Nora stops writing em dashes, and sounds less like an assistant when she names you, teases you, or signs off.
details: The em dash was the measurable tell. On one Discord window (Langfuse trace `0cfb9fea`, 2026-09-21) she used one in 13 of her 22 messages; the people in the same 40-message window used none in 18. The cause was in her INPUT, not her instruction: the doctrine showed her 44 em dashes and the context-block descriptions another 42, on every single turn, while the file that governs how she sounds never mentioned the mark. An instruction cannot win 1:86 against a demonstration, so both halves moved. Every em dash is now gone from all five doctrine files and from every served block description, and voice.md states what a chat pause IS (a comma, a full stop, or two messages) rather than what it is not, because a «do not use X» lead has been measured to raise the odds of X rather than lower them.

voice.md also gained the two positions behind the rest of the complaint, and grew by 487 tokens doing it. Naming somebody is an act, not an opener: she opened on the operator's nickname in 13 of 22 replies, because that nickname was the single piece of personalisation her prompt gave her, and a model handed one hook pulls it every turn. And a tease is made of what is in front of her and is spent once used: she made the same joke about the hour on two adjacent turns, having reached for the clock because the clock was the only live, specific fact she had. The banned customer-service ending was widened from the PHRASE to the MOVE, since 8 of 22 replies still ended by offering to do more, just wearing a question mark.

conduct.md and constraints.md were compressed by deleting restatement, not rules. Three pairs of sections in conduct each said one thing twice; constraints said the picture rules three times. conduct.md is also now written in ENGLISH throughout: it describes what she DOES, so which language a clause happened to be in recorded who wrote it and when, and nothing else. voice.md stays Cantonese because that file IS a specimen of the register it teaches, and quoted speech stays Cantonese everywhere, because an utterance is a specimen too. Measured on one tokenizer, conduct's body went 2,781 -> 2,312 (compression) -> 2,217 (English); the language change on its own is roughly token-neutral, and the saving is the compression. constraints 1,234 -> 1,107. Every clause the content tests pin is still present, which is the point: what came out was duplication.

NOT MEASURED: whether any of this changes what she writes. The dash count in what she READS is a fact; the dash count in what she SAYS needs the eval suite and is still owed. DEC-78/DEC-92's finding that prose alone has not been shown to move behaviour is not overturned here.

AUDITED, and the compression claim failed. Kimi 0.40.1 was given the before and after of both files with one instruction, to falsify «I deleted restatement, not rules». It found eight behavioural rules deleted rather than restated, all restored: the retrieve-before-you-accuse procedure in the verdict section, which is the highest-stakes place she attributes words to a person and which the banter section's anti-fabrication rule does not reach; holding an open thing as undecided rather than acting as though it closed; «pick what fits the moment rather than what performs», which is the clause that governed the over-teasing this release is partly about; «wrong practical advice costs more than a flat joke», the tie-breaker that says which way to err; what she could not check staying unchecked on LATER turns; not performing a familiarity she does not have, of which the invented-preference rule is only the narrowest instance; not re-arguing the defence after conceding; and in constraints the literal placeholder syntax, which is a recogniser rather than a repertoire. One mistranslation was corrected: 「唔講點解 fit」 is an ARTICULATION duty and the English had softened it to an existence condition. The audit also caught a collision this release introduced, where voice.md's list of occasions to name somebody omitted the one conduct.md mandates; that list is now a default plus a test instead. After the restorations the doctrine is 6,443 tokens against 6,312 before, so the honest result is that conduct.md was not 20% compressible. It was compressible by the amount of genuine duplication, which is much smaller, and the first two passes bought their saving by deleting rules classified as restatement.
